packages.name: nomad_sdk.identity
packages.description:
``nomad_sdk.identity`` — credentials for NOMAD, in the style of ``azure.identity``.

A credential is any object with ``get_token() -> AccessToken``. Clients only ever ask
a credential for a token; how the token is obtained (a personal access token, the
Keycloak password grant, environment variables) is the credential's business::

    from nomad_sdk import NomadClient
    from nomad_sdk.identity import EnvironmentCredential

    client = NomadClient('test', credential=EnvironmentCredential())

Nothing here reads the environment or the network at import time.

members.name: AccessToken
members.description: A bearer token and when it expires (Unix time; ``inf`` = not known to expire).

members.name: EnvironmentCredential
members.signature: EnvironmentCredential(*, api_url: str | None = None, env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None)
members.description:
Credential configured by environment variables, read when it is created.

* ``NOMAD_PAT`` → :class:`PersonalAccessTokenCredential` (preferred);
* otherwise ``NOMAD_USERNAME`` + ``NOMAD_PASSWORD`` →
  :class:`UsernamePasswordCredential` on ``api_url`` or ``NOMAD_API_URL``.

raises.description: none of the variables is set.

members.name: PersonalAccessTokenCredential
members.description:
A NOMAD personal access token (PAT), or any pre-issued bearer token.

The recommended credential for scripts, notebooks and CI. Create a PAT in the
NOMAD GUI (see nomad-docs ``howto/manage/program/auth.md``).

members.name: TokenCredential
members.description: Anything that can produce a bearer token for NOMAD.

members.name: UsernamePasswordCredential
members.signature: UsernamePasswordCredential(username: str, password: str, *, api_url: str, timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S, session: requests.Session | None = None)
members.description:
Username and password, exchanged for a short-lived token on ``/auth/token``.

Kept for users coming from ``nomad-utility-workflows``; prefer a PAT.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: NOMAD username.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: NOMAD password.

parameters.name: api_url
parameters.description:
The deployment that issues the token (URL or alias such as
``test``); use the same deployment as the client.

packages.name: nomad_sdk.api
packages.description:
``nomad_sdk.api`` — a Python client library for NOMAD.

It wraps NOMAD's REST API the way ``boto3`` or the Azure SDKs wrap theirs: you work
with a client, operation groups and typed models, never with URLs or HTTP::

    from nomad_sdk import NomadClient
    from nomad_sdk.identity import PersonalAccessTokenCredential

    client = NomadClient('test', PersonalAccessTokenCredential(pat))
    me = client.users.get_me()

Credentials live in :mod:`nomad_sdk.identity`, errors in :mod:`nomad_sdk.exceptions`.

members.name: NomadClient
members.signature: NomadClient(api_url: str, credential: TokenCredential | None = None, *, timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S, session: requests.Session | None = None)
members.description:
Client for one NOMAD deployment.

Operations are grouped by resource: ``client.users`` today; ``uploads``,
``entries`` and ``datasets`` follow. Methods return typed models from
:mod:`nomad_sdk.api.models` and raise :mod:`nomad_sdk.exceptions` errors.

parameters.name: api_url
parameters.description:
API v1 base URL, or a deployment alias (``central``, ``test``,
``develop``).

parameters.name: credential
parameters.description:
Any :class:`~nomad_sdk.identity.TokenCredential`, e.g.
:class:`~nomad_sdk.identity.PersonalAccessTokenCredential`. Omit it
for anonymous access to public data.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Per-request timeout in seconds.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Optional pre-configured ``requests.Session`` (proxies, retries).

packages.name: nomad_sdk.workflow
packages.description:
``nomad_sdk.workflow`` — build NOMAD custom-workflow archives.

The current public API is the engine ported from ``nomad-utility-workflows``:
describe nodes with :class:`NodeAttributes`, turn them into a graph with
:func:`nodes_to_graph`, and let :class:`NomadWorkflow` fill default inputs/outputs
and write ``workflow.archive.yaml``.

A higher-level, object-oriented builder is planned for a later milestone; it will
compile down to this engine, so code written against these names keeps working.

members.name: NodeAttributesUniverse
members.description:
Container for all node attributes in a NOMAD workflow graph.

This class holds a mapping from node keys (integers) to their corresponding
`NodeAttributes` objects, representing the full set of nodes in a workflow.
It is used as the input for building the workflow graph and for serializing
or deserializing workflow definitions.

members.description:
Represents a NOMAD workflow and provides methods to build and serialize it.

This class manages the workflow graph, node attributes, and the logic for
constructing a NOMAD-compatible workflow archive. It supports registering
nodes, resolving edges, adding default sections, and exporting the workflow
to a YAML file for use with NOMAD systems.

parameters.description: The root section of the archive to store the workflow.

members.name: build_workflow_yaml
members.description:
Construct and serialize the workflow archive to a YAML file.

This method registers all nodes in the workflow graph as sections, builds the
internal task elements, generates the workflow archive, removes duplicate
inputs/outputs, and writes the resulting archive to the YAML file specified by
`self.destination_filename`. The resulting YAML file is compatible with the
NOMAD workflow schema and can be used for further processing or import into
NOMAD systems.

After writing the file, a summary message is logged with the output filename.
